facts.statement: The genus name Shuvuuia comes from the Mongolian word for bird.
facts.quote: The name Shuvuuia is derived from the Mongolian word shuvuu (шувуу) meaning "bird".

facts.statement: Shuvuuia measured about 1 meter in length and weighed approximately 3.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: At 1 m in length and 3.5 kg in body mass, it is one of the smallest known non-avian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Shuvuuia had long, slender hindlimbs with short toes that likely allowed for significant running speed.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs of Shuvuuia were long, slender, and short-toed, which may indicate significant running capabilities.

facts.statement: Shuvuuia possessed unusually short but powerfully built forelimbs.
facts.quote: The forelimbs, however, were unusually short and powerfully constructed.

facts.statement: Newer specimens reveal that Shuvuuia had a massively enlarged thumb plus reduced second and third fingers, contrary to earlier beliefs of a single digit.
facts.quote: Although originally Shuvuuia and other alvarezsaurids were thought to have only a single digit on the front limb, newer specimens show the presence of reduced second and third fingers in addition to the massively enlarged thumb known from previous specimens.

facts.statement: Shuvuuia fossils are found in the Djadochta Formation of Mongolia, dating to about 75 million years ago during the late Campanian.
facts.quote: Fossils of Shuvuuia are currently known from two locations within the Djadochta Formation: Ukhaa Tolgod and Tögrögiin Shiree. These sites are thought to be about 75 million years old (late Campanian age).

facts.statement: Shuvuuia likely used its strong forelimbs to open insect nests and its mobile jaws to probe for prey.
facts.quote: Like other alvarezsaurids, Shuvuuia may have used its forelimbs to open insect nests, and its slender, unusually mobile jaws to probe after such prey.

facts.statement: A Shuvuuia fossil was found surrounded by tube-like structures resembling the central shafts of modern bird feathers.
facts.quote: Specimen IGM 100/977 of Shuvuuia was found surrounded by small, hollow, tube-like structures resembling the rachis (central vane) of modern bird feathers.

facts.statement: Biochemical analysis of feather-like structures on a Shuvuuia specimen confirmed it likely possessed a coat of feathers.
facts.quote: While beta-keratin is found in all integumentary (skin and feather) cells of reptiles and birds, only bird feathers completely lack alpha-keratin. These findings show that, though poorly preserved, Shuvuuia likely possessed a coat of feathers.

facts.statement: Shuvuuia was the fourth non-avian dinosaur to show direct evidence of feathers.
facts.quote: Shuvuuia fue el cuarto dinosaurio no aviar en mostrar evidencias directas de la presencia de plumas.

facts.statement: Shuvuuia belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae, known for short, powerful forelimbs specialized for digging.
facts.quote: It is a member of the family Alvarezsauridae, small coelurosaurian dinosaurs which are characterized by short but powerful forelimbs specialized for digging.

facts.statement: Shuvuuia is classified within the family Alvarezsauridae.
The genus Shuvuuia was described by Chiappe, Norell, and Clark in 1998.
Shuvuuia lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2025 study rejected the hypothesis that Shuvuuia had owl-like hearing, arguing that the measurement method compared braincase depths that differ significantly between basal theropods and modern birds.
facts.quote: However, these conclusions were rejected by a study in 2025. It was objected that the lagena relative size had been measured by a comparison to the braincase depth, which however with basal theropods was much lower than in modern birds.

rejected.statement: Shuvuuia could flex its upper jaw independently of its braincase, a trait unique among non-avian theropods.
rejected.quote: Shuvuuia is unique among non-avian theropods in the skull's ability to perform prokinesis; that is, it could flex its upper jaw independently of its braincase.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'could flex its upper jaw independently of its'

rejected.statement: Research suggests Shuvuuia was an owl-like nocturnal hunter that used its legs to chase prey and its arms to dig small animals from burrows, though this hypothesis was rejected in 2025.
rejected.quote: However, new research based on analysis of the theropod's ears suggests that it was actually an owl-like, nocturnal hunter which used its strong legs to run down prey, and its arms to dig small prey such as insects and mammals out of burrows and shrubs
